target_equation: $S = \frac{I_g G}{I - I_g},\quad R_s = \frac{V}{I_g} - G,\quad R_A \to 0,\quad R_V \to \infty$
starting_principles: Kirchhoff's Current Law (conservation of charge): $\sum I_{\text{in}} = \sum I_{\text{out}}$
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (conservation of energy): $\sum \Delta V = 0$ around any closed loop
Parallel branch voltage equality: components in parallel share identical potential drop
assumptions: D'Arsonval moving-coil galvanometer has linear angular response with internal coil resistance $G$ and full-scale deflection current $I_g$
Shunt resistor $S$ and multiplier resistor $R_s$ are ideal ohmic resistors with zero temperature drift
External connecting wires have negligible resistance

ordered_steps.description: Establish parallel circuit configuration and current division for ammeter conversion.
ordered_steps.operation: Express shunt current as $I_S = I - I_g$ and equate potential drops across parallel branches: $V_S = V_G$
ordered_steps.result_equation: $I_S S = I_g G \implies (I - I_g) S = I_g G$
assumptions_applied: Kirchhoff's current law at the input node

ordered_steps.description: Isolate the required shunt resistance $S$ to measure a maximum current $I$.
ordered_steps.operation: Divide by $(I - I_g)$ and define the current multiplication factor $n_I = \frac{I}{I_g}$

ordered_steps.description: Compute the equivalent resistance of the shunted galvanometer and deduce the ideal ammeter condition.
ordered_steps.operation: Solve for equivalent resistance $R_A = \frac{G S}{G + S}$ and take the limit as desired measurement capability $I \to \infty \implies S \to 0$
ordered_steps.result_equation: $R_A = \frac{G S}{G + S} < S;\quad \lim_{S \to 0} R_A = 0 \implies V_A = I R_A = 0$
assumptions_applied: Zero insertion perturbation condition for non-invasive series measurement

ordered_steps.description: Establish series circuit configuration and voltage division for voltmeter conversion.
ordered_steps.operation: Express potential drops using common series current $I_g$ at full-scale deflection
ordered_steps.result_equation: $V = I_g R_s + I_g G = I_g(R_s + G)$

ordered_steps.description: Isolate the required series multiplier resistance $R_s$ to measure a maximum potential difference $V$.
ordered_steps.operation: Divide by $I_g$, subtract $G$, and define the voltage multiplication factor $n_V = \frac{V}{I_g G}$
assumptions_applied: Voltage range extension requirement $V > I_g G$

ordered_steps.description: Compute the total internal resistance of the converted voltmeter and deduce the ideal voltmeter condition.
ordered_steps.operation: Take the limit as target full-scale voltage $V \to \infty \implies R_s \to \infty$
assumptions_applied: Zero loading perturbation condition for non-invasive parallel measurement

final_equation: $S = \frac{I_g G}{I - I_g},\quad R_s = \frac{V}{I_g} - G,\quad R_A \to 0,\quad R_V \to \infty$
applicability_conditions: Valid for linear DC moving-coil galvanometers
